events.title: Andrew Tanenbaum creates MINIX
events.summary: Andrew Tanenbaum created MINIX in 1987 — a teaching [microkernel] [OS] that inspired Linus Torvalds to build Linux.
events.about: Tanenbaum's textbooks and MINIX shaped [OS] education worldwide. The famous Tanenbaum–Torvalds [microkernel] debate defined architectural trade-offs developers still argue about.

narrative.whyChosen: MINIX was the direct inspiration for Linux's initial design.
narrative.whyImportant: It made operating system source code accessible to students.
narrative.problemSolved: Unix source was proprietary and unavailable for classroom study.

events.title: Game cracking group Fairlight (FLT) founded
events.summary: The warez group Fairlight — known by the tag FLT — formed in 1987 and became legendary for cracking [PC] and Amiga games with cinematic intro demos.
events.about: Fairlight's cracktros paired reverse-engineering skill with demoscene aesthetics — trainers, keygens, and removed copy protection shipped hours after retail releases. Groups like FLT, SKIDROW, and RELOADED kept pace with SecuROM, Denuvo, and online DRM — an arms race that pushed anti-tamper technology and shaped how game publishers think about authentication.

narrative.whyChosen: Fairlight's FLT tag is iconic in game-cracking and demoscene crossover culture.
narrative.whyImportant: Scene cracks were the benchmark that forced stronger DRM and always-online checks.
narrative.problemSolved: This was unauthorized copying — it revealed how fast skilled reversers could defeat commercial protection.
